screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin (diphenylhydantoin) monotherapy in patients with psychomotor (focal) epilepsy.

Randomised trial comparing phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy in newly diagnosed epileptic patients. While primary outcome was cognitive function, it meets inclusion criteria as an RCT comparing the two drugs.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis synthesizing data from multiple trials, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Randomised pragmatic trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs including phenytoin and carbamazepine as monotherapy in adults with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures.
Methodological paper discussing principles of equivalence trial design, not a primary clinical trial.
Prospective observational cohort study examining factors associated with refractory epilepsy, not a randomised controlled trial comparing carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Review article discussing principles of AED therapy, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Observational study examining cognitive function changes with various AEDs, not a randomised controlled trial comparing carbamazepine versus phenytoin monotherapy.
Animal study examining phenytoin-folate interactions in rats, not a human randomised controlled trial.
Randomised pragmatic trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs including phenytoin and carbamazepine as monotherapy in children with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures.
Epidemiological survey estimating prevalence/incidence of neurologic disorders, not a randomised controlled trial.

Study evaluating carbamazepine added to existing combination therapy in institutionalized patients with uncontrolled seizures, not a head-to-head comparison of carbamazepine versus phenytoin monotherapy.
Population-based epidemiological study of epilepsy incidence, not a randomised controlled trial.
Multi-center double-blind randomised trial comparing carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, and primidone as monotherapy in adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
Review article discussing epidemiological research methods in epilepsy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Observational study examining somatosensory evoked potential changes with phenytoin or carbamazepine, not a randomised controlled trial comparing efficacy of the two drugs.
Population-based prospective incidence study of epilepsy in Iceland, not a randomised controlled trial.
Methodological paper describing statistical methods for meta-analysis, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Meta-analysis estimating global burden of epilepsy, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Position paper presenting updated ILAE classification of epilepsies, not a randomised controlled trial.
Double-blind randomised study comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin (diphenylhydantoin) monotherapy in patients with temporal lobe (focal) epilepsy.
Review article discussing phenytoin uses and side effects in dermatology, not a randomised controlled trial.
Double-blind crossover randomised trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin monotherapy in patients with focal and major generalized seizures.
Randomised trial comparing carbamazepine, phenytoin, and sodium valproate monotherapy in children with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Includes direct comparison of carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Basic science study examining GABA receptor modulation in cell cultures, not a clinical randomised controlled trial.
Pharmacokinetic study of zonisamide and its interactions with other AEDs, not a randomised controlled trial comparing carbamazepine versus phenytoin monotherapy.
Basic science study examining sodium channel inhibition in neuroblastoma cells, not a clinical randomised controlled trial.
Methodological guideline paper introducing PRISMA statement for reporting systematic reviews, not a clinical trial.
Double-blind study comparing multiple anticonvulsants including phenytoin but does not include carbamazepine in the comparison.
Network meta-analysis of individual participant data from multiple trials, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Observational case series of children experiencing seizure exacerbation with carbamazepine, not a randomised controlled trial.
Cochrane review protocol examining congenital malformation outcomes, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Case series of children with aberrant seizure reactions to carbamazepine, not a randomised controlled trial.

Double-blind crossover randomised trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin monotherapy in patients with uncontrolled partial and generalized epilepsy. Primary outcome was EEG changes but meets inclusion criteria.
Clinical Q&A article discussing carbamazepine safety in pregnancy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Prospective randomised study comparing carbamazepine, phenytoin, and phenobarbitone monotherapy in Nigerian patients with epilepsy. Includes direct comparison of carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Observational study examining serum zinc and copper levels in patients on various AEDs, not a randomised controlled trial comparing carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Controlled trial of carbamazepine but abstract does not clearly indicate comparison with phenytoin monotherapy.
Prospective trials of phenytoin and carbamazepine but does not appear to be a randomised controlled trial design; rather observational follow-up of patients treated with each drug.
Prospective observational study examining congenital malformations in children exposed in utero to AEDs, not a randomised controlled trial.
Double-blind crossover randomised trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin (diphenylhydantoin) monotherapy in epileptic patients.
Cochrane review protocol examining neurodevelopmental outcomes, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Methodological paper discussing IPD meta-analysis approaches, not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Prospective registry study examining congenital malformation risks, not a randomised controlled trial.
Methodological paper about measuring inconsistency/heterogeneity in meta-analyses, not a clinical trial.
Methodological study examining outcome reporting bias in Cochrane reviews, not a primary clinical trial.
Historical population-based incidence study of epilepsy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Case series of adults developing absence seizures with carbamazepine therapy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Basic science study examining sodium channel inhibition in mammalian cell lines, not a clinical randomised controlled trial.
Longitudinal observational study describing natural history of epilepsy, not a randomised controlled trial.
Counterbalanced crossover randomised trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin monotherapy in adult epileptics, assessing psychotropic effects.
Cochrane review comparing phenobarbitone versus phenytoin, not carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Record linkage study examining risk of cutaneous reactions, not a randomised controlled trial.
Prospective community-based cohort study identifying prognostic factors for remission, not a randomised controlled trial.
Randomised trial comparing phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy in newly diagnosed adult epileptic patients, assessing cognitive effects.
Randomised trial comparing phenobarbital versus phenytoin, not carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Methodological paper describing statistical methods for meta-analysis, not a clinical trial.
